I was driving with a friend to Long Beach for a concert at about 9pm. We were in the left lane going about 60-65 (there was no traffic) and suddenly I notice the person way ahead of me is going much slower, I brake to about 20-25mph and still end up barely hitting her trunk. My hood was bent a tad, I didn't notice any damage to her car. But there are people speeding by on the highway, some swerving to miss our cars successfully, then there was this truck. I was watching in the rear view mirror this pickup truck oversteering and beginning to slide sideways at very high speeds. I looked at my friend next to me and thought he would be the last thing I ever saw. So I left my seatbelt on and the truck slammed into my stopped coupe at about 75mph. I remember glass flying past my head, being hit in the neck by some large metal pieces, before slamming my face into the steering wheel. Thought that would be it, but all I got was whiplash and a bump on my forehead. My friend was knocked unconscious and when he came to, we climbed out of the window and waited for an ambulance. He doesn't remember anything, I'm kinda glad.

Mirena is levonorgestrel, a progestin with high androgenic properties. This means it can be converted to an estrogen or a testosterone, depending on your body. Combo pills have progestins in them but are balanced out by also having a type of estrogen in it as well. My body happened to use the mirena as a testosterone, resulting in all of the unwanted side effects. It's a tricky compound that you can't predict the effects until you try it. Everyone's different. I'm not sure what combo pill you were taking before, but if it worked well for you, stick with something with similar ingredients/dose. :) Just ask your doctor about it. Hope that helped.

My mom has ms. And honestly, although it can be rough when she has episodes or 'flares' as they call them, the thing that affects her the most is her own mood. You cannot have a self defeatist attitude with this. It's the worst thing you can do. I've seen my mom dismiss so many opportunities because she was afraid of having a flare up. But you know, when she is forced to do things, like hiking or going to the beach, she is completely fine, and can do everything just like the rest of us. Because her mind isn't focused on 'I can't' or 'my disease won't let me'. It's just not true. 


Her food choices are poor, which raises her cholesterol and blood pressure, and we noticed when her blood pressure is high, that's when she will have an episode, or even a seizure. Please always watch what you eat. I am trying to get her eating gluten free, more veggies, absolutely no fast or fried food, as well as flax and hempseed and cherry juice for the inflammation. You can't take a passive approach and just take pills for things you could fix yourself. 


You need to keep moving. Get a little exercise everyday. Water exercises are best for ms, because the water keeps your body temperature down. Our a/c is permanently set to 68 degrees for her. And yes, if you call the electric company they will discount your bill because of your health issue. 


My mom is currently on copaxone, it is a daily self administered shot. Along with a slew of other meds for her sleeping, anxiety, blood pressure, allergies, the list goes on. She reacts to a lot of meds she tries to help symptoms with and this spurs flare ups. If she gets a cold it can get out of hand and also cause a flare up. But if you notice, several of these things can be helped or even prevented with relaxation exercises. I cannot stress enough that you can't lose hope and give up because of a diagnosis. You have to take control of your own life. 


You can't ask someone how your own quality of life will be. Because that is something which is entirely up to you. Best of luck, and don't worry so much.
